# `exec` check

Run a command and judge it by exit code and output, or let it report its own result as JSON.

```yaml
checks:
  example:
    type: exec
    command: [pg_isready, -h, db.internal]
    expect:
      exit: 0
```

## Keys

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | list of string |  | Program and arguments, run directly without a shell, e.g. [pg_isready, -h, db]. Set exactly one of command or shell. |
| `shell` | string |  | Command line run by sh -c (cmd /c on Windows), for pipes and redirects. Set exactly one of command or shell. |
| `env` | map of string |  | Extra environment variables for the command. |
| `cwd` | string |  | Working directory. |
| `output` | one of: text, json | `text` | text: judge by exit code and expect. json: the command prints {"status": "passed\|warning\|failed", "message": ..., "details": {...}} on stdout. |
| `expect` | mapping |  | What counts as healthy (output: text only). |
| `expect.exit` | integer | `0` | Required exit code. |
| `expect.stdout_contains` | string |  | Text stdout must contain. |

Every check also accepts the [common keys](../config.md#common-check-keys).

One-liner: `medic check exec <shell> [--set key=value ...]`
